adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — The matcher checks characters 3-4 and rejects equality, so event tests accept token IDs carrying the wrong grant shortcut and can go green while encoding is broken.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:82 — Comparing only the two map sizes misses combined ID-and-shortcut collisions, allowing ambiguous grant mappings to survive startup validation and decode token context inconsistently.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that comparing map sizes misses 'combined ID-and-shortcut collisions'. Looking at the code, the validation checks if grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size(). The maps are built by iterating over all OAuth2GrantType factories and adding entries to both maps - grantsByShortcuts maps shortcut->grantName and grantsToShortcuts maps grantName->shortcut. If two grants have the same shortcut, grantsByShortcuts would have fewer entries (due to key collision), making sizes differ. If two grants have the same ID, grantsToShortcuts would have fewer entries. The size comparison actually does catch duplicate shortcuts or duplicate IDs. The finding's concern about 'combined ID-and-shortcut collisions' is unclear - if grant A has shortcut 'ab' and grant B has ID 'ab', these go into different maps with different key spaces, so there's no collision issue. The validation is correct for its purpose.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Adding a mandatory getShortcut method makes existing third-party grant factories fail with AbstractMethodError during encoder post-initialization unless the method has a backward-compatible default.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface adds a new abstract method `getShortcut()` without a default implementation. This is a breaking change for any existing third-party implementations of OAuth2GrantTypeFactory - they will fail with AbstractMethodError at runtime when the method is called. The DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() method iterates over all OAuth2GrantType providers and calls getShortcut() on each factory, which would trigger this error for any third-party grant type that hasn't been updated. A backward-compatible default implementation should be provided.

server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Requiring every grant factory to expose the default token encoder's compact shortcut leaks one encoding strategy into the generic grant SPI and burdens all custom grant implementations.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that adding getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory (a generic SPI interface) couples all grant implementations to a specific encoding strategy used by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider. The diff shows this new abstract method is added to the interface and must be implemented by all grant factories (AuthorizationCodeGrantTypeFactory, ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory, etc.). This is a valid architectural concern - the shortcut is specifically used for token ID encoding in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, but the requirement is pushed to the generic grant SPI. Custom grant implementations would need to provide shortcuts even if they don't use this encoding. This is a legitimate design/scope concern grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109 — Grant-type propagation is manually duplicated across issuance paths, so every new or bypassing flow must remember hidden context setup or silently emits an unknown grant marker.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that grant-type propagation is manually added in multiple places across the diff: OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.java:134, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.java:82, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237, and TokenManager.java:248. Each grant flow must manually set `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...)`. This is a valid architectural concern - if a new grant type is added or an existing flow is modified without this manual setup, it will silently use 'unknown' grant marker. This is a legitimate design/maintainability issue grounded in the diff, though not a bug since the current implementation works correctly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:74 — Calling the newly abstract getShortcut() on every grant factory makes existing binary-compatible custom grant providers throw AbstractMethodError during postInit and prevents server startup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface has a new method `getShortcut()` added (lines in OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java). In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), the code iterates over all OAuth2GrantType provider factories and calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on each one. Since this is a new abstract method in the interface with no default implementation, any existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations that were compiled against the old interface will not have this method, causing AbstractMethodError at runtime when postInit() is called during server startup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:39 — The tests manually seed factory maps and only parse handcrafted IDs, leaving SPI initialization and real token grant/session context propagation unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the unit test in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java manually seeds the factory maps (grantsByShortcuts, grantsToShortcuts) with hardcoded values rather than testing the actual SPI initialization flow. The test creates a factory, calls init(null), then manually populates the maps. This means the postInit() method which loads grants from the actual OAuth2GrantType providers is never tested. While the encoding/decoding logic is tested, the integration with real grant type factories and session context propagation is not covered by this unit test. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic.
